questions.q: What's the relationship between the report body's size on the design surface and the physical page size?
options: Physical page size only matters for HTML rendering, never for PDF or Print
They are always identical — resizing one always resizes the other
They're separate concepts — the report body is elastic with no inherent size limit, while the physical page is fixed and is what hard page-break renderers actually paginate against
The physical page size is determined automatically from the report body's size
questions.explain: The report body grows or shrinks to fit its contents with no ceiling, but the physical page (default 8.5x11 inches) is fixed and is what PDF, Image, and Print renderers actually paginate against.

questions.q: Where do you set page size and margins so the settings are saved permanently into the report definition?
options: In the Report Data pane's New menu
Page size and margins cannot be set inside Report Builder at all
Only in Run mode's Page Setup, which is the sole location for margins
Right-click the gray area around the design surface, select Report Properties, then Page Setup
questions.explain: Design-mode settings (via Report Properties → Page Setup) are saved into the report definition; Run-mode Page Setup settings are session-only and revert when the report is reopened.

questions.q: What happens to a report item that extends into the margin area?
options: The report throws an error and fails to render
It automatically resizes to fit within the margin
Margins have no visible effect on rendering
It gets clipped in hard page-break renders — the overlapping part simply doesn't render
questions.explain: Margins are measured inward from the physical page edge, and content extending into that margin area is clipped rather than rendered.

questions.q: What's a concrete technique for keeping a wide matrix from spilling onto extra pages when printed?
options: Switch the dataset's query type from Text to Table
Narrow columns to only what's needed, shorten headers, and consider rotating a label column's text 270 degrees
Matrices cannot be made print-friendly under any circumstances
Increase the report body's width until it matches the widest possible column count
questions.explain: These are the same fixes introduced in Lesson 9 for matrices: resize columns down to only what's needed, rename long headers, and use WritingMode = Rotate270 to reclaim horizontal space.

questions.q: Which view actually simulates the printed, paginated page, rather than the flexible, non-paginated design surface?
options: Print Layout, accessed from the Run tab
The Grouping pane
The default design view, at all times
The Report Part Gallery pane
questions.explain: Print Layout, available from the Run tab once you're previewing, is the only view that actually simulates how the report will paginate when printed or exported to a hard page-break format.
